question: What is the primary goal of safe motherhood initiatives regarding maternal health?

options.A: To eliminate the need for postnatal care completely
options.B: To ensure women receive necessary care to reduce maternal and neonatal mortality
options.C: To restrict childbirth strictly to tertiary medical centers
options.D: To focus exclusively on the nutritional status of the fetus

explanation: Safe motherhood initiatives aim to ensure that all women receive necessary care throughout pregnancy, childbirth, and the postpartum period to significantly reduce maternal and neonatal morbidity and mortality. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h1)

question: Why is the role of the nurse particularly critical in primary health care centres during prenatal services in Nigeria?

options.A: Nurses are usually the primary point of contact for expectant mothers
options.B: Nurses handle all financial budgeting for the hospital
options.C: Nurses are responsible for building maternity wards
options.D: Nurses replace the need for physician consultations entirely

explanation: Nurses often serve as the primary point of contact for pregnant women seeking care in primary health care centres, making their understanding of prenatal care essential. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h1)

question: According to current WHO guidelines, what is the recommended minimum number of contacts for a pregnant woman during routine antenatal care?
explanation: The World Health Organization recommends a minimum of eight contacts during antenatal care to reduce perinatal mortality and improve the mother's experience of care. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h2)

question: Which of the following best describes the principle of cultural sensitivity in antenatal care?

options.A: Ignoring cultural practices entirely in favor of strict biomedical models
options.B: Respecting local beliefs while using empathetic education to address harmful practices
options.C: Adapting all medical treatments to align with traditional medicine without question
options.D: Restricting pregnant women from expressing their cultural beliefs in clinics

explanation: Cultural sensitivity requires nurses to respect local beliefs and practices while gently discouraging harmful traditional behaviors through empathetic health education. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of the initial prenatal booking visit?

options.A: To schedule the date of delivery definitively
options.B: To establish a baseline health profile and identify pre-existing risk factors
options.C: To administer the final doses of routine immunizations
options.D: To discharge the patient from active clinic follow-up

explanation: The initial visit establishes a baseline health profile, estimates gestational age, and identifies any pre-existing medical or obstetric risk factors. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h3)

question: In the Nigerian healthcare context, which preventive medication is typically initiated during the early prenatal visits to combat a major endemic disease?

options.B: Intermittent preventive treatment for malaria using sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine
options.C: Prophylactic antibiotics for urinary tract infections
options.D: High-dose chemotherapy for gestational trophoblastic disease

explanation: Malaria screening and the initiation of intermittent preventive treatment in pregnancy (IPTp) with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine are vital components of the initial visit in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h3)

question: Which vital sign is monitored at every routine follow-up visit primarily to screen for gestational hypertension and pre-eclampsia?
explanation: Blood pressure is assessed at every follow-up visit specifically to screen for gestational hypertension and pre-eclampsia. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h4)

question: What is the clinical purpose of measuring symphysis-fundal height during follow-up abdominal examinations?

options.A: To estimate the exact blood volume of the mother
options.B: To correlate fundal growth with gestational age
options.C: To determine the exact date of conception
options.D: To measure the mother's pelvic outlet dimensions

explanation: Symphysis-fundal height is measured in centimeters to correlate with gestational age and monitor proper fetal growth. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h4)

question: Why are iron and folic acid supplements routinely prescribed during prenatal care?

options.A: To prevent maternal insomnia and depression
options.B: To prevent nutritional anemia and neural tube defects
options.C: To accelerate the closure of the maternal fontanelles
options.D: To induce labor contractions during the third trimester

explanation: Iron and folic acid are routinely prescribed to prevent nutritional anemia in the mother and neural tube defects in the developing fetus. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h5)

question: Which of the following is considered an obstetric danger sign that requires immediate medical attention?

options.A: Mild dependent ankle edema at the end of the day
options.C: Sudden severe headache and blurring of vision
options.D: Gradual weight gain appropriate for gestational age

explanation: Severe headache and blurring of vision are classic danger signs indicating potential pre-eclampsia, which requires immediate hospital presentation. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h5)

question: What medication is commonly administered in hospital settings to manage severe pre-eclampsia and prevent eclamptic seizures?
explanation: Magnesium sulfate is the drug of choice for managing severe pre-eclampsia and preventing or treating eclamptic seizures. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h6)

question: Which of the following interventions helps prevent neonatal tetanus through maternal immunization during pregnancy?

options.D: Giving high doses of Vitamin A

explanation: Tetanus toxoid vaccine is routinely administered to pregnant women to stimulate antibody production that protects both the mother and newborn against tetanus. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h6)

question: What does the strategy of Birth Preparedness and Complication Readiness (BPCR) primarily help families plan for?

options.A: The child's secondary school education fund
options.B: Logistics such as a skilled birth attendant, facility, transportation, and emergency funds
options.C: The naming ceremony and cultural celebrations
options.D: The purchase of infant formula and bottles

explanation: BPCR planning ensures families identify a skilled birth attendant, a designated health facility, transportation, emergency funds, and blood donors in case of complications. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h7)

question: When should exclusive breastfeeding ideally be initiated following childbirth?

options.A: Within the first hour of life
options.B: After the first 24 hours of life
options.C: Only when the milk turns white after colostrum is discarded

explanation: Exclusive breastfeeding should ideally be initiated within the first hour of life to promote bonding, provide colostrum, and ensure successful lactation. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h7)

question: Why is the antenatal card held by the pregnant woman considered critically important in emergency situations?

options.A: It serves as a health insurance card for purchasing groceries
options.B: It provides a portable, detailed medical history for clinicians at any facility
options.C: It exempts the patient from paying hospital utility bills
options.D: It replaces the need for verbal communication entirely

explanation: The antenatal card serves as a portable medical history, ensuring clinicians at any receiving facility have immediate access to vital clinical data. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h8)

question: What is an essential step when executing a patient referral from a primary health clinic to a tertiary hospital?

options.A: Discharging the client without any accompanying records
options.B: Stabilizing the client and ensuring proper communication and documentation
options.C: Waiting until the next scheduled clinic day to send the patient
options.D: Instructing the family to manage transport entirely without notifying the receiving facility

explanation: A robust referral requires stabilizing the client, clear communication, proper documentation, and ensuring safe transfer without delays. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h8)
